newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - BBN up on GTE bid.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - BBN up on GTE bid.

text.p: Shares in Internet-service provider BBN Corp climbed 6-3/8 to 29 preceding Tuesday's market open, the price in-line with GTE Corp's friendly bid for the company announced this morning, traders said.
GTE made no moves in early third market trade, they said.
Under terms of the $616 million deal, GTE will start a cash tender offer for BBN "shortly" according to GTE.
GTE also announced a strategic alliance with Cisco Systems Inc to develop enhanced data and Internet services.
Stock in Cisco, due to announce quarterly earnings later today, slipped 1/4 to 58-3/8 before the open, traders said.
Philip Morris Cos Inc slipped 1/2 to 43-1/2 while RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp shares were untraded before the market open. RJR closed at 32-5/8 Monday.
Both stocks soared in afternoon trade yesterday after a Florida jury ruled RJR's R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co unit was not negligent in the death of a former smoker.
Duramed Pharmaceuticals Inc went into a freefall in pre-open trade, tumbling to 4-1/2 from 10-3/8.
Trader said fall was driven by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's decision Monday to not approve Duramed's synthetic generic form of the estrogen-replacement drug Premarin.
America Online traded down to 50-1/8 before the market open from 51-1/4.
The company reported fiscal third quarter profits of $0.02 per share last night, above the analysts' consensus forecast of a $0.07 per share loss.
AOL earned $0.14 per share in the year-ago period.
